topics.title: Matter and Atomic Structure
topics.objective: Describe particles, atomic structure, isotopes and electron arrangements for the first twenty elements.

topics.title: The Periodic Table

topics.title: Stoichiometry

topics.title: Reactions, Rates and Energetics
topics.objective: Explain rates of reaction using collision theory, interpret reversible reactions and calculate enthalpy changes.

topics.title: Acids, Bases and Salts
topics.objective: Describe acid and alkali properties, neutralisation reactions and the preparation of pure salts.

topics.title: Metals and Reactivity

topics.title: Organic Chemistry
topics.objective: Identify homologous series, functional groups and reactions of alkanes, alkenes, alcohols, acids and polymers.

topics.title: Electrolysis

topics.title: Experimental Techniques and Chemical Analysis
topics.objective: Select tests to identify gases, cations and anions and interpret chromatography results.

questions.prompt: Chlorine exists naturally as two isotopes, ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl. Answer the following questions about these isotopes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.correctAnswer: Atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.

parts.text: State the numbers of protons, neutrons and electrons in one atom of ³⁷Cl.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why ³⁵Cl and ³⁷Cl have identical chemical properties.
parts.correctAnswer: Chemical properties depend on the electron arrangement; both isotopes have 17 electrons and the same arrangement, so they react identically.

questions.correctAnswer: (a) atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons; (b) 17 protons, 20 neutrons, 17 electrons; (c) identical electron arrangements give identical chemical properties.
questions.workedSolution: (a) Isotopes are atoms of the same element (same proton number) with different nucleon numbers because they contain different numbers of neutrons. (b) Chlorine has proton number 17, so every chlorine atom has 17 protons and, being neutral, 17 electrons; neutrons = 37 − 17 = 20. (c) Chemical reactions involve only the outer electrons; both isotopes have the configuration 2,8,7, so they behave identically. The extra neutrons change only the mass.

questions.prompt: A sample of chlorine contains 75% of the isotope ³⁵Cl and 25% of the isotope ³⁷Cl. Calculate the relative atomic mass of the chlorine in the sample.
questions.workedSolution: Relative atomic mass = (percentage × mass number) for each isotope, summed, divided by 100: (75 × 35 + 25 × 37) ÷ 100 = (2,625 + 925) ÷ 100 = 3,550 ÷ 100 = 35.5. Answer: the relative atomic mass is 35.5.

questions.prompt: Sodium reacts with chlorine to form sodium chloride, NaCl. Answer the following questions about the bonding and properties of sodium chloride.
questions.contentLabel: Original BrillaPrep practice material aligned to the published Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620) syllabus; not official Cambridge International material and not official WAEC material. Use the enabled feedback channel to report corrections.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe, in terms of electrons, how a sodium atom becomes a sodium ion.
parts.correctAnswer: A sodium atom (2,8,1) loses its one outer-shell electron to form a Na⁺ ion with the full outer shell 2,8.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: State the type of bonding present in sodium chloride.
parts.correctAnswer: Ionic bonding — the electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain why sodium chloride has a high melting point.
parts.correctAnswer: It forms a giant ionic lattice with strong electrostatic attractions between ions in all directions; a large amount of energy is needed to overcome these attractions.

questions.correctAnswer: (a) the sodium atom loses its outer electron to form Na⁺; (b) ionic bonding; (c) strong electrostatic attractions throughout the giant lattice need much energy to overcome.
questions.workedSolution: (a) Sodium has the electron arrangement 2,8,1; losing the single outer electron leaves the stable arrangement 2,8 and the ion Na⁺. (b) The transfer of electrons from sodium to chlorine produces oppositely charged ions, so the bonding is ionic. (c) In the solid lattice every ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions; the strong attractions extend in all directions, so a lot of heat energy is required to separate the ions, giving a high melting point.
